answer: Under collision-pair proof-of-work admission, each identity joining the tundra relay is admitted only by publishing a nonce making the hash of its identity-key collide with the hash of one specific other same-epoch applicant assigned by a public deterministic prism shuffle, and each applicant-slot can be a partner at most once, so n fake violet agents must find n(n−1)/2 distinct collisions: 1,000 sybils require about 499,500 puzzle solutions, while an honest agent needs exactly one partner and one ~2^20 hash, roughly 0.0002% of the attacker's per-head burden.
